# #6073 -- Non-const static data members of templated structs fail to compile

## Verdict: `repros`

Still broken on `main` (`89e2f98e2`, self-reports `1.9.0.5465 (triage, 7665270b9)`)
and on every stable release that can even parse HLSL templates,
**v1.7.2308 through v1.9.2607 (12 releases, linear scan, no invalid probes
inside that range)**. HLSL template support did not exist before v1.7.2308
(older releases answer `'template' is a reserved keyword in HLSL`, an
`invalid-probe`, not a clean result -- see below), and v1.7.2308 is the
release the reporter filed against (1.7.2308.12), so the probeable history
covers the issue's entire life with no gap.

## Repro

Reconstructed from the issue body's quoted "Actual Behavior" text (the three
linked shader-playground.timjones.io URLs could not be fetched from this
environment) and from the maintainer's own public
[cpp.godbolt.org repro](https://cpp.godbolt.org/z/E5Yxj5qYv), whose exact
stored HLSL source and DXC args were pulled through Compiler Explorer's
`shortlinkinfo` API (`compilers: dxc_trunk, options: "-T cs_6_6 -fcgl"`) rather
than approximated from the page's client-rendered HTML:

```hlsl
template<int ID>
struct Test
{
    static int Num;
};

template<int ID>
int Test<ID>::Num = 2;

RWBuffer<int> MyBuffer;

[numthreads(1,1,1)]
void main(uint3 DispatchThreadId : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
   MyBuffer[DispatchThreadId.x] = Test<42>::Num;
}
```

`cmd.txt` uses `-T cs_6_0` (no `-fcgl`) rather than the maintainer's
`cs_6_6 -fcgl` -- confirmed to reproduce identically (see
out-main-debug.txt) and it widens the profile compatibility for release
binaries that predate SM 6.6. Repro quality: **agent-constructed but
independently corroborated** -- the compiled mangled name
`i32* @"\01?Num@?$Test@$0CK@@@2HA"` is **byte-identical** to the one quoted in
the issue body, so `Test<42>::Num` reconstructs the reporter's own
instantiation, not merely the same class of bug.

## The reported symptom, reproduced exactly, on stable release binaries

On downloaded v1.7.2308 and v1.9.2607 (`out-v1.7.2308.txt`,
`out-v1.9.2607.txt`), the repro exits `0x80004005` (E_FAIL, an ordinary
diagnosed-error exit, not a crash by `is_internal_failure()`) with stderr:

```
Declaration may not be in a Comdat!
i32* @"\01?Num@?$Test@$0CK@@@2HA"
```

This is LLVM's IR-verifier text, quoted **verbatim** in the issue body. Every
one of the 12 probeable stable releases (v1.7.2308..v1.9.2607) produces this
identical text.

## One defect, two signatures (Debug ground truth vs. Release)

The Debug `main-debug` ground truth does **not** show this text on a plain
run -- it crashes first, before ever reaching the verifier:

```
Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert
```
exit `0xE0000001` (`out-main-debug.txt`), from a Debug-only assert in
`clang::LinkageComputer::getLVForDecl`
(`tools/clang/lib/AST/Decl.cpp:1357`, `assert(!Old || Old->getCachedLinkage()
== D->getCachedLinkage())`).

Continuing past that Debug-only assert under `cdb` with `gh` ("go handled" --
emulating NDEBUG, i.e. what a Release build does since `assert()` is a no-op
there) shows the **same Debug binary**, on the **same input**, then reach the
exact Comdat text quoted above, before `error: LLVM ERROR: Broken module
found, compilation aborted!` (`manual-case-gh-continue.txt`, generated by
`measure-gh-continue.py`). This establishes that the Debug-only assert and
the reported Release-build symptom are the same underlying defect, not two
unrelated bugs that happen to share a repro -- the assert just fires first
because Debug builds keep the check compiled in.

`match.json` is therefore `any_of[contains("may not be in a Comdat"),
internal_failure]`: the text clause is what the Release-style manifestation
needs (E_FAIL is explicitly excluded from `is_internal_failure()`, by design,
since it's also the exit code for ordinary diagnosed errors), and the
`internal_failure` clause is what the Debug ground truth's earlier crash
needs.

## Controls

Both patterns the issue itself says already work were re-tested and score
`no-repro` under this predicate, confirming it discriminates correctly and
does not fire on the surrounding working cases:

- `control-nontemplate.hlsl` -- identical static-member pattern, no template
  (`variant-control-nontemplate-main-debug.txt`, exit 0).
- `control-templateconst.hlsl` -- templated struct, but the static member is
  `const` (`variant-control-templateconst-main-debug.txt`, exit 0).

## Bisection

```
python scripts/triage.py bisect --issue 6073 --linear
```

`invalid-probe` (feature absent, "'template' is a reserved keyword in HLSL")
on v1.4.1907 through v1.7.2212.1 -- 8 releases, HLSL templates simply did not
exist yet. `repro` on every probeable release from v1.7.2308 through
v1.9.2607 (12 releases: v1.7.2308, v1.8.2403, v1.8.2403.1, v1.8.2403.2,
v1.8.2405, v1.8.2407, v1.8.2502, v1.8.2505, v1.8.2505.1, v1.9.2602,
v1.9.2602.24, v1.9.2607). Five probeable prereleases outside the search
(v1.5.2003, v1.8.2306-preview, v1.8.2405-mesh-nodes-preview, v1.10.2605.2,
v1.10.2605.24) are excluded from the search by policy (not explicitly named
by this issue). No fix has ever shipped: `always-repro'd`.

## Compiler Explorer

https://godbolt.org/z/17nh9j5fW -- `dxc_1_6_2112` (CE's oldest DXC, predates
HLSL templates entirely, not evidence either way) and `dxc_trunk`, which
fails with `LLVM ERROR: Broken module found, compilation aborted!` (CE's pane
does not surface the intermediate "Declaration may not be in a Comdat!" line
that the local release binaries print, only the final abort -- noted in
`godbolt-note.txt`). CE runs a Release Linux build and corroborates the local
measurement; it does not overrule it.

## Labels

Current: `bug`, `crash`, `correctness` -- all still accurate (this is a real
crash-shaped internal failure that impacts shader correctness). Proposing to
add `hlsl-next`: the maintainer's own comment says the durable fix likely
needs "changing the language in the future to avoid these kinds of
collisions" between HLSL's static/global codegen and C++ template
instantiation, which is exactly what that label describes.

## What was not established

- No source-level fix commit exists to attribute a boundary to -- this has
  never worked on any release that can parse the repro, so there is nothing
  to bisect a *fix* from.
- No maintainer follow-up beyond the one 2023-11-30 comment; no linked PR
  (`gh api .../timeline` returns zero cross-references).
- Whether every non-const-static-in-template shape fails the same way, or
  only ones producing a Comdat-eligible declaration, was not explored beyond
  the reporter's and maintainer's own repro; not needed for this verdict.
